 Column Headings:

   TT date: Calendar date of greatest eclipse (TT time-scale). Gregorian
            after and including 1582-Oct-15; Julian before and including
            1582-Oct-04.

 TT GE (M): Time of greatest eclipse (TT time-scale at centre of Moon).

      Type: PNP 1 = Penumbral Partial
            PNT 2 = Penumbral Total
            UMP 3 = Umbral Partial
            UMT 4 = Umbral Total
            UMC 5 = Umbral Central

     Gamma: Minimum distance attained by shadow-axis from centre of Moon
            (lunar radii). Positive if north of centre; negative if south.
            Time of event equal to greatest eclipse.

      Pmag: Penumbral magnitude at greatest eclipse
            (fraction of the lunar diameter obscured by the penumbra).

      Umag: Umbral magnitude at greatest eclipse
            (fraction of the lunar diameter obscured by the umbra).

       Lun: Lunation number (Lunation #0 starting on 2000-Jan-06).

       Sar: Saros number.

       Inx: Inex number.

     P4-P1: Duration P1 --> P4 in minutes.

     U4-U1: Duration U1 --> U4 in minutes.

     U3-U2: Duration U2 --> U3 in minutes.

        P1: Time of first external contact with the Earth's penumbra
            (hours from the time of greatest eclipse).

        U1: Time of first external contact with the Earth's umbra
            (hours from the time of greatest eclipse).

        U2: Time of first internal contact with the Earth's umbra
            (hours from the time of greatest eclipse).

        U3: Time of last internal contact with the Earth's umbra
            (hours from the time of greatest eclipse).

        U4: Time of last external contact with the Earth's umbra
            (hours from the time of greatest eclipse).

        P4: Time of last external contact with the Earth's penumbra
            (hours from the time of greatest eclipse).

  eLngW GE: Ephemeris longitude (west) of sub-lunar point on the Earth
            at the time of greatest eclipse (degrees).

    Lat GE: Geodetic latitude (WGS84) of sub-lunar point on the Earth
            at the time of greatest eclipse (degrees).

       ELT: Earth light-time in seconds (strictly between the centre of the
            Moon and the sub-lunar point on the Earth at the time of greatest
            eclipse).
